solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shortest possible gathering devoted to French cheese?

parts.note: Brie is a soft cheese from France
a fest is a festive gathering, as in a beer fest

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek suggestion for a festival devoted entirely to Brie.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as a second, whimsical definition: a 'Brie fest' would be a gathering devoted to the cheese; 'devoted to' simply links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of brief, meaning the most short in duration possible.

clue.text: In punt, request a picnic hamper?

indicators.note: the word request is placed in the middle of the gamble word, splitting it

parts.note: a punt is a wager, a bet
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone on a punting trip asks for the picnic hamper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' suggests the flat-bottomed boat used on the Cam and Isis, but here it is a gamble, BET.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a wicker container, a classic example of the woven carrier type.

clue.text: Lacking interest, fall liable to debts?

parts.note: to incur something is to become liable to it
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs indifferently at the prospect of running up debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone without curiosity shows no interest in finding things out.

clue.text: Flourish provisions for keen supporters?

parts.note: fans are keen supporters; the word is used attributively here, as in fan mail
fare means food or provisions

explanation.surface: A flourish of trumpets, or catering for enthusiastic followers.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as food laid on for fans; 'for' is a link joining the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A flourish in the musical sense is a short ceremonial burst of trumpets.

clue.text: Puncture made by small parasite

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tick is a blood-sucking parasite

explanation.surface: A tiny puncture wound left by a biting parasite.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce or prick something is to puncture it.

clue.text: Actor theatre brought back to pen lyric

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the theatre word wraps around the lyric
the repertory theatre word is read from end to start

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
a lay is a short lyric poem or song

explanation.surface: An actor returns to the theatre to write a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like writing, but it means enclose: the turned-round theatre word goes around the lyric.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a performer who takes a role on stage.

clue.text: Quantity of light batter has to stay in the same condition, right?

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash

parts.words: to stay in the same condition
parts.note: 'let it be' means leave it as it is, so be means continue unchanged

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: light batter must keep its consistency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light batter' looks like a cooking ingredient, but 'Quantity of light' is the definition and 'batter' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of luminance in physics, named after Johann Heinrich Lambert.

clue.text: Long period of time before November

parts.note: a year is a period of time
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Waiting a long time until November comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective about the period, but it is the verb meaning to crave.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave or pine for it.

clue.text: Change one's mind about note being suggestive

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the yielding word goes around the musical note

parts.note: to relent is to soften and change one's mind
do (doh) is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders a remark that seemed a bit suggestive.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent of something means evocative or reminiscent of it.

clue.text: Man in check cap

indicators.note: the staffing word sits inside the halting word

parts.note: to check something is to stop it
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A chess-like phrase: a man in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man in check' suggests chess, but 'Man' is the verb to staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A threaded lid that twists onto a bottle or jar is a kind of cap.

clue.text: Nearly all money got from subsidiary job by male with deputy

indicators.note: nearly all means the final letter of the phrase is lost

parts.note: earnings from a second job are a second income
and means with, joined together

explanation.surface: Someone takes a side job alongside a man and his assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly all' drops the last E of SECOND INCOME, leaving SECONDINCOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the officer next in authority below the leader, who stands in when needed.

clue.text: Designate weapon to be carried by English ship

indicators.note: the weapon word is held within the English-and-vessel pair

parts.note: an ark is a ship, as Noah's
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: Choose a weapon to be loaded on board an English vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something aside for a particular purpose is to designate it.

clue.text: Perennial outside's no cross

indicators.note: no means without, so the cross is removed from the outside word

parts.note: external means outside
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about a perennial plant with no cross on its exterior.
explanation.definitionFit: Perennial means lasting for ever or recurring endlessly, i.e. everlasting.

clue.text: A rolling county

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for a somersault, a head-over-heels roll

explanation.definitionFit: The old word for a somersault is also the name of a south-west English county.

clue.text: Drink that's small for each, without ostentatious luxury

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the each-word goes around the luxury word

parts.note: per means for each
ritz, as in 'putting on the ritz', means ostentatious luxury, from the Ritz hotels

explanation.surface: A modest drink each, with no showy extravagance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixture of white wine and soda water is a long drink.

clue.text: Tons come down to exercise

parts.note: rain comes down from the sky

explanation.surface: Heavy rain arrives just as it's time to exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise in order to get fit or drill a skill is to practise or school.

clue.text: Coffee giving out nice aroma

indicators.note: giving out suggests the letters breaking down and coming apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A cup of coffee giving off a pleasant smell.
explanation.definitionFit: An espresso diluted with hot water is a style of coffee.

clue.text: Birds start to turn in attempt to take off

indicators.note: the bird word and opening letter go inside the attempt word

parts.note: a try is an attempt
Aves is the zoological class of birds

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Birds begin to wheel round as they try to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like flight but is the noun take-off, a parody.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque parody or mockery of something is a send-up.

clue.text: Change state support to include energy

indicators.note: the support word takes in the energy letter

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a snooker cue
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A government altering state support to cover energy bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state support' looks like welfare, but 'state' belongs with 'Change' in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To return a device or setting to its starting condition is to restore it.

clue.text: Step on public transport: request stops early

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport

indicators.note: stops early means the word is cut short before its end

parts.note: a plea is a request

explanation.surface: A passenger request to stop early on public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops early' drops the last A of PLEA, leaving PLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush underfoot is to step heavily on something.

clue.text: Ravel preludes caused dislike

indicators.note: to ravel is to tangle, so the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Ravel's preludes caused distaste among listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' looks like the French composer, but it is the verb, to tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsed means disgusted or sickened, i.e. filled with distaste.

clue.text: Left Western Europe for part of West Africa

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula of Spain and Portugal in western Europe

explanation.surface: Someone leaves Western Europe for West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A country on the Atlantic coast of West Africa, founded by freed American slaves.

clue.text: Part of Bible's there?

indicators.note: part of says the letters are a portion of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a passage is in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an Old Testament book, part of the Bible, sits in 'Bible's there'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Testament book, telling of the Jewish queen of Persia, is a portion of scripture.

clue.text: Gallons carried out in barrel for homeless

indicators.note: the gallons letter and running word go in the barrel word

parts.note: a vat is a large barrel
to run a scheme is to carry it out, past tense ran

explanation.surface: Gallons carried out in a barrel, perhaps by a rough sleeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no settled home and wandering is the vagabond's life.

clue.text: Causes of disease resistance in cat's eyes, perhaps

indicators.note: the resistance letter goes inside the gemstone word

parts.note: cat's eye is a gemstone, so gems by example
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A vet investigates disease resistance in a cat's eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat's eyes' suggests a pet's eyes; it is the gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Microbes that bring on illness are the pathogens behind infection.

clue.text: Buns nibbled in fancy bars

indicators.note: the nibbling word is put inside the reordered bars
fancy as a verb means to imagine, so the letters are reimagined in a new order

parts.note: bit is past tense of bite, i.e. nibbled

explanation.surface: Bread buns nibbled in elegant bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buns' looks like bakery fare and 'fancy' like an adjective; 'fancy' is the anagram signal and 'Buns' is a pet name for the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Bun is an affectionate pet name for a bunny, so buns are these long-eared animals.

clue.text: Weapon force used during upset

indicators.note: the force letter is used in the middle of the upset word

parts.note: to rile is to upset or annoy
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: A weapon and force are used during a disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-barrelled gun is a firearm.

clue.text: Poor being made to pay for strikes?

definitions.text: being made to pay for strikes?
definitions.meaning: strapped can mean beaten with a strap, so a strapping given in return for money

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for having very little money is literally to be short of it.

clue.text: Unlikely refusers of Arab country importing ultimate in arms

indicators.note: importing means bringing in, so the country takes in a letter

parts.note: Yemen is a country on the Arabian peninsula

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of the next word, the last one

explanation.surface: An Arab country importing the latest arms is unlikely to refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophants who always agree with their boss are the last people to say no.

clue.text: Argue excessively in boozy Blue Boar

indicators.note: boozy means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Drinkers at a pub called the Blue Boar argue too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blue Boar is a typical British pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: To labour a point is to dwell on it at tedious length.
